hops.title: Compare it: a green jacket over a yellow shirt
hops.text: After your colour test, zip a green jacket over a yellow shirt and ask what is hiding underneath. A leaf does something similar: green chlorophyll covers yellow and orange colours that sit inside the leaf all summer. When fall days get shorter, the green fades away. You can still recognise the leaf by its shape.

sources.citation: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry, Why Leaves Change Color
U.S. National Park Service, Why Do Leaves Change Colors in the Fall

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A partly unzipped green jacket showing a yellow shirt, beside a green maple leaf and an orange maple leaf of the same shape.
image.caption: Green chlorophyll covers yellow and orange colours all summer, like a green jacket over a yellow shirt.

hops.title: Say it: you found the leaf's drinking straws
hops.text: "Whoa, you just found the leaf's drinking straws!" Say it the moment bumpy lines appear on the rubbing. Those raised veins really do carry water and nutrients through the leaf, and their pattern, along with shape and edges, can help you tell trees apart. Keep small broken crayon bits away from children under four, because they are a choking risk.

sources.citation: University of Illinois Extension, Great Plant Escape: Plant Parts, Leaves

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A green leaf next to a blue crayon rubbing on white paper that shows branching leaf veins, with a peeled crayon nearby.
image.caption: A rubbing shows the leaf's veins, the tiny pipes that carry water and nutrients.

hops.title: Point at it: twigs that grow in pairs or one at a time
hops.text: On your next walk, stay close and look up at twigs together, no pulling on branches. Maple leaves grow straight across from each other in pairs, like outstretched arms. On white oaks and most other trees, leaves join the twig one at a time. In winter, the buds along the sides of the twig follow the same pattern.

sources.citation: Virginia Tech Dendrology, Basics of Tree ID: Leaf Arrangement
Virginia Tech Dendrology Fact Sheet, White Oak (Quercus alba)
OpenKey (ibiblio), Quercus alba: leaves alternate or spiral

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A parent and child seen from behind on a park sidewalk, looking up at a maple twig with paired leaves and a white oak twig with single leaves at staggered spots.
image.caption: Look up together: maple leaves grow in pairs, while white oak leaves join the twig one at a time.
